requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: If the from field contains more than one mailbox specification (including all mailboxes included in any groups), then the sender field, containing the field name "Sender" and a single address, MUST appear in the message.

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: The from field and the sender field SHOULD NOT use group syntax; rather, the from field SHOULD use only the mailbox-list syntax and the sender field SHOULD use only mailbox syntax (see RFC 6854, Section 3).

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: If the sender field uses group syntax, the group MUST NOT contain more than one mailbox.

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: In either case, an optional reply-to field MAY also be included, which contains the field name "Reply-To" and a comma-separated list of one or more addresses.

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: If the originator of the message can be indicated by a single mailbox and the author and transmitter are identical, the "Sender:" field SHOULD NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: In the absence of the "Reply-To:" field, replies SHOULD by default be sent to the mailbox(es) specified in the "From:" field unless otherwise specified by the person composing the reply.

requirements.heading: Replacement of RFC 5322, Section 3.6.2. Originator Fields
requirements.text: In all cases, the "From:" field SHOULD NOT contain any mailbox that does not belong to the author(s) of the message.

requirements.heading: Applicability Statement
requirements.text: In particular, user agents SHOULD NOT permit the use of groups in those fields in outgoing messages.
